title: Combined Financing Limit and Application of Payments Across Ridgeline Accounts
content:
Financing under Ridgeline Home Improvement Financing is limited across the customer's whole portfolio as well as per plan.

## 1. Combined limit on opening an account

A new account is opened only when the customer's combined financed amount across open accounts, including the new one, stays within the combined limit. The combined financed amount is the total of the financed amounts on the customer's financing accounts whose status is approved, active or delinquent, read from the company's financing records before the account is opened; the combined limit is the plan's figure for the most a customer may have financed across all open accounts together.

## 2. Which account a payment is applied to

A payment is applied to the account whose account number the customer gives and is never split across accounts. When the customer does not name one, it is applied to the account with the earliest past-due payment, and otherwise to the account with the earliest next due date.

## Payment application at a glance

| Customer names an account number | Some account has a past-due payment | Account the payment is applied to |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | — | The account named |
| No | Yes | The account with the earliest past-due payment |
| No | No | The account with the earliest next due date |

In every row the whole payment goes to one account.

## Hypothetical illustration of the combined limit

Suppose a hypothetical combined limit of L. A customer with open accounts financing amounts A and B may open a new account financing C only when A, B and C together stay within L; the financed amount of a paid-off or cancelled account does not count, because only approved, active and delinquent accounts enter the total.
